19:			{Key: keymap.Copy, Description: "Copy the command under Run to the clipboard, whole. DevDesk never runs it (detail)"},
29:			{Key: "ctrl+p", Description: "Open command mode"},
40:				Body:  "Vulnerability Scan: detects CVEs in dependencies and packages (Trivy).
Secret Scan: runs both scanners, and the Secrets tab shows their findings together. Gitleaks reads a repository's working tree and git history; Trivy reads the target's content, which is what gives an image a secret scan at all — Gitleaks cannot scan one. The Source column says which tool found each finding.
Misconfig Scan: detects IaC misconfigurations in Dockerfiles, Terraform, Kubernetes manifests and Helm charts (Trivy). On the Misconfigurations tab, the Source column shows the dialect each finding comes from.
K8s schema: validates a repository's Kubernetes manifests against the API schema of the configured Kubernetes version (kubeconform) — a wrong type, an unknown field, an apiVersion that release no longer serves. Its findings are on the Misconfigurations tab, with 'schema' as their source. Helm charts and Kustomize overlays are never validated raw — a template is not YAML until it is rendered. When helm is available, each chart is linted ('helm lint') and rendered, then validated; when kustomize is available, each overlay is built, then validated. A finding from a rendered resource points at its template or its kustomization, with no line. Without either tool, the results header counts them as Not rendered.
Build context: DevDesk's own check, run with the Misconfiguration category and needing no tool. A Dockerfile at the repository's root whose final image copies the whole context (COPY . or ADD .) is reported when that context holds a .git directory, or files such as .env, *.pem, *.key, id_rsa, credentials.json or .npmrc, that no .dockerignore leaves out — the git history, and a secret committed then deleted with it, would be readable from the image's layers. Only what is certain is reported: a .dockerignore pattern DevDesk cannot read, or one that may bring part of .git back, means silence. A Dockerfile below the root is not checked, since its build context is not written anywhere; the log says so. Its findings have 'context' as their source.
Base image signatures: DevDesk's own check too, run with the Misconfiguration category unless Verify image signatures is unticked (scan tab of the configuration view). Every FROM of every Dockerfile — a build stage included, since a compromised builder writes the binary that ships — is checked against your rules (~/.devdesk/trust.yaml) and the built-in ones, with cosign. A signature by an unexpected identity is CRITICAL (DEVDESK-SIG-001); no accepted signature where a rule requires one is HIGH (DEVDESK-SIG-002). Only a proven violation is a finding: an image no rule covers says nothing, and a check that could not run under one of your rules is reported as an error of the scan. Its findings have 'signature' as their source, and the Remediation tab lists candidates whose signature holds.
License Scan: analyzes dependency licenses (Trivy).
CI Score: grades a repository's pipeline configuration (plumber), for this context's forge only — a repository hosted elsewhere is not graded rather than graded without credentials. The grade is on the CI tab, above the issues; a run that could not collect everything says so instead of showing a letter.",
52:				Body:  "Results are displayed by tab (CVE, Secrets, Licenses, Misconfig). Every finding belongs to exactly one tab, and the count on each label is the same number the scan recorded. Severity is filtered with c, h, m and l — they are cumulative, so c and h together ask for CRITICAL or HIGH, which a threshold could not express. The active ones are shown in the bar under the table, beside the search field. '.' cycles the sort column and '/' searches. The Fixable figure in the header counts the vulnerabilities that have a fixed version, split into base image packages (cleared by upgrading the image's packages or moving to a newer base image) and application dependencies (cleared only by bumping the dependency itself); a result scanned before this was recorded shows its findings as unclassified until the next scan. On the Misconfigurations tab a File column shows where each finding is, as a path relative to the scanned directory (a path under the scanner container's /scan mount is shortened to its relative form, and any other absolute path under your home directory starts with ~); it is the first column dropped on a narrow terminal, and a long path loses its start, not its file name. Press Enter to view finding details (see Finding details), which name the package kind and the command that moves it. For secrets, X adds a finding to .gitleaksignore; it is offered for Gitleaks findings only, since that file is matched on a Gitleaks fingerprint a Trivy secret does not have.
Esc returns to the inventory, or to the list the results were opened from.",
58:					"Under Fix, with no blank line: Where is the file and line, then the package, the CI job, its script line and the matched text when the finding has them. Do is the numbered steps, then the resolution the scanner gave, word for word. Run is the command, on one line, cut with an ellipsis when it is wider than the column; DevDesk shows it and never runs it. A sentence such as 'Update foo to 1.2', for an ecosystem DevDesk has no command for, is a step under Do, never a command. Effect is what the fix does, or 'Fixed in <version>', and Warning is what the built-in fix may break.
" +
60:					"The detail has six keys, the same for every finding, each greyed with its reason in the footer when it has nothing to act on. Esc goes back. W opens the first reference. Enter opens the finding's file in the viewer (O there opens the IDE, esc comes back to the detail); whether the file exists is for the viewer to say, and a path outside the scanned directory, or a target that is an image, is refused. Ctrl+O applies the built-in fix of this finding, with the same preview, the same confirmation that defaults to No, the same write and the same re-scan as the Misconfigurations tab; while the re-scan runs the footer says so, and when it ends the detail shows the finding as the re-scan read it, or closes if the finding is gone, with the verdict in the footer. Y copies the command under Run to the clipboard, whole even when the screen cuts it; DevDesk never runs a command. X adds a Gitleaks secret to .gitleaksignore, after a confirmation. Each acts on the finding on screen, not on the row behind it.

73:				Body: "For a repository, this tab reads the Dockerfiles under it and lists each base image — every stage, since a vulnerability in a build stage can reach the image that ships — with the newer tags it could move to. Candidates keep the image's variant (alpine stays alpine, slim stays slim) and its precision (3.18 is offered 3.21, not 3.21.1); by default they stay on the same major version, and the scan tab of the configuration view (Base image bumps) lets them take the next one.
Nothing is measured until you press S: each image is scanned straight from its registry, without being pulled, and the counts are kept for 24 hours. The vs now column is the change in CRITICAL plus HIGH against the image as written; negative is better. A candidate is a proposal with its evidence — the scan says the CVEs are gone, not that the application still runs on the new base.
The Update column puts an arrow on a base image whose registry has something newer: a later patch tag, or new content behind the same tag (the arrow alone — a new build) — compared with the digest the Dockerfile pins, or with the image the engine holds under that name; one the engine does not hold only gets the patch side, and shows a cloud (not local). The other states, each an icon: a check mark (up to date), an hourglass (no answer yet), a question mark in a circle (the registry did not answer), a pin (a digest with no tag, which cannot move). The registries are asked in the background when the tab opens, and each answer is kept 6 hours.
A floating tag — latest, an untagged reference, main, a codename, or a vendor tag rebuilt in place such as Docker Hardened Images' — has no version to move to, so it lists no candidates and says so. Its count is of what the tag pointed to when it was scanned, and the registry may have replaced that since: S scans it again every time, whatever its age, rather than trusting the 24 hours. Nothing is written for it — pinning it by digest would stop it following upstream fixes.
An image scan has no Dockerfile, so the tab is empty for one.
Choosing: space picks the candidate under the cursor for its stage — only one that has been scanned, since a bump is proposed with its evidence — and Enter shows what the choices would change. Ctrl+O writes them, and only when you ask: it lists each file and line, and says what git will be able to undo (a clean tracked file can be reverted with git checkout; one with uncommitted changes cannot without losing them; an untracked file or one outside a repository cannot at all). The answer defaults to No. Only the image reference changes — comments, line endings and the rest of the file are untouched — and DevDesk makes no commit, branch or push. A file that changed since the diff was computed is refused, not overwritten. A reference pinned by digest loses its pin, which the modal says. A stage that reads its image from an ARG changes that ARG's default, and a --build-arg on the command line can still override it.
" +

Les cinq points sont corrigés, avec un test écrit et vu rouge avant chaque correctif. `gofmt -l` est vide, `mise run lint` donne 0 issue (host et windows), `go test -count=1` passe sur security, scan, keymap, theme, app et remediation, et `mise run ci` sort avec le code **0** (test-race inclus). Rien n'est commité.

**1. « Re-scanning… » sans fin.** Une erreur du re-scan (échec ou arrêt par `K`, qui passe par un `InventoryScanFinishedMsg` avec `Err`) remet maintenant `misconfigVerifying` à nil. Je n'ai pas dérivé le statut du registre de jobs : le snapshot peut arriver après l'écriture et ferait clignoter le statut. Le `case` d'`Update()` appelle `handleScanFinishedForFix` (Rule 201). Le footer d'erreur de l'inventaire reste affiché. Tests : `details_verify_test.go` (échec, arrêt, scan d'une autre cible sans effet). `WantsBlink()` repasse à false.

**2. Commande copiée.**
- (a) `scan.FixCommand` valide `pkg` et `version` contre `[A-Za-z0-9@/._+~:=^,-]+`, sans tiret initial. Les entrées valides gardent leurs octets (test sur les formes npm scopé, module Go, epoch/revision Debian, `+build`). Pour une valeur refusée, `trivyFixCommand` retombe sur la phrase « Update … » existante.
- (b) `runCommand` refuse, en plus de `\n` : tout caractère de contrôle, tout caractère non imprimable ou blanc autre qu'un espace simple, et les 17 métacaractères demandés. J'ai ajouté `!unicode.IsPrint`, qui couvre aussi NBSP, U+2028, les marques bidi (U+202E) et le zero-width space. Dans ce cas, pas de ligne Run et Y est grisé avec `reasonNoCommand`.
- (c) `fixSteps` met sous Do tout `FixCommand` que `runCommand` refuse, y compris multi-ligne. L'affichage retire les caractères de contrôle (point 4).
- Tests : 30 commandes piégées, dont espaces suivis de `; rm -rf`, ESC, `\r`, tab et multi-ligne (`details_command_safety_test.go`, `fixcommand_safety_test.go`).

**3. Liens symboliques.** `findingFilePath` reste pur (la Rule 130 est respectée). La Cmd d'enter appelle `staysInside`, qui applique `EvalSymlinks` au chemin et à la racine puis refait le test Rel. Un lien qui sort de la cible renvoie `FindingFileRefusedMsg`, affiché en Warn avec `reasonFileLinkOutsideTarget`. Un fichier absent reste au viewer, et un lien qui reste dans la cible est ouvert. Le viewer reçoit le chemin d'origine. Tests : lien vers un dossier et vers un fichier extérieurs, lien intérieur, chemin inexistant, lien cassé (`details_symlink_test.go`).

**4. ESC / C0 / C1.** `withoutControlSpace` (utilisé par `normalizeText` et `oneLine`) supprime les séquences CSI/OSC avec `ansi.Strip`, puis les caractères de contrôle, U+2028/2029 et les caractères de format (bidi, zero-width). Il garde `\n`, transforme le tab en 4 espaces et garde ZWJ/ZWNJ pour les emoji. Tests : `details_control_test.go`, y compris un finding dont tous les champs (Message, File, Job, Script, Description, etc.) portent un OSC.

**5. Doc.** `docs/architecture/scanning.md` couvre : la liste blanche, `runCommand` et `shellMeta`, le texte du scanner, les liens symboliques (avec la fenêtre TOCTOU), la fin du statut de re-scan, et les limites de `sameFinding`. Le texte d'aide `GetHelpContent()` est aussi mis à jour. Aucune touche ne change.

**Écarts et points ouverts**
- Un re-scan arrêté pendant qu'il est en file d'attente, ou l'arrêt du run depuis `:jobs`, n'émet aucun message : le statut « Re-scanning » reste affiché. Je l'ai noté dans la doc comme lacune connue, sans correctif.
- Il reste une fenêtre TOCTOU entre la vérification des liens et l'ouverture par le viewer, car le viewer ouvre par chemin. C'est documenté.
- J'ai écrit les tests de `details_control_test.go` après le correctif du point 4. J'ai ensuite remis l'ancienne fonction un instant : ils échouent, puis repassent avec le correctif.
- Un nom de package hostile donne une phrase « Update … » qui reprend le texte brut, affiché nettoyé sous Do et non copiable.

Fichiers modifiés (sous `.worktrees/feat/sec-detail-fix-block-751/`)
- `internal/scan/fixcommand.go`
- `internal/ui/security/details_fix.go`
- `internal/ui/security/details_actions.go`
- `internal/ui/security/details_text.go`
- `internal/ui/security/update.go`
- `internal/ui/security/misconfig_write.go`
- `internal/ui/security/header.go`
- `docs/architecture/scanning.md`

Nouveaux tests (même racine)
- `internal/scan/fixcommand_safety_test.go`
- `internal/ui/security/details_verify_test.go`
- `internal/ui/security/details_command_safety_test.go`
- `internal/ui/security/details_control_test.go`
- `internal/ui/security/details_symlink_test.go`
